source.title: Layer-wise Target Propagation: Efficient Component Attribution through Target Centric Propagation
source.authors: Lasse M. Jantsch; Dong-Jae Koh; Seonghyeon Lee; Young-Kyoon Suh

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates component attribution on IOI and reports specific limits: its logit-level approach misses negative name-mover effects, and its IOI results include approximation errors. It also compares LTP rankings with exact activation patching, but does not identify or test the original 26-head circuit.
record.gate_note: IOI component-ablation and recovery results, plus an exact activation-patching comparison of head rankings, bear on IOI attribution. The study does not test the named GPT-2 Small circuit, its seven head classes and roles, backup-head self-repair, or prompt-variant generality. Its broader comparisons of attribution methods are not recorded unless they report an IOI component result.
record.test_reason: This is a methods paper. IOI serves as a benchmark for scoring the authors' attribution method (LTP) against other attribution baselines, and the patching comparison only validates LTP's rankings. No result identifies the IOI circuit's heads, classes or roles, or tests backup heads, cross-model circuit reuse, method-independence of a recovered circuit, or prompt variants. The remark that logit attribution misses negative name-mover heads is a limitation of LTP, not a measurement of the circuit.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct, with one omission. The record leaves out that LTP is not best on IOI in several settings. Attn-only scores a higher IOI total on Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-4B, and AtP scores higher recovery on GPT-2 Large IOI. The authors explain the IOI dip by logit-level attribution and approximation error in IOI's specialized circuit.
record.recipe_differences: LTP propagates a target backward through linearized transformer pathways; the original study identifies and tests a specific GPT-2 Small circuit using circuit-focused interventions and criteria. This paper uses component attribution and zero-ablation/recovery evaluations, with a limited comparison to exact activation patching.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors note that logit-level attribution misses suppressive effects, zero ablation may create out-of-distribution artifacts, and LTP's IOI attribution has approximation errors. They report different agreement levels for causally effective heads versus the full attention-head population.

fits_no_version.finding: On IOI, LTP's component-ranking faithfulness relative to other attribution methods varies by model. Attn-only beats it on Llama-3.1-8B (total 92.92 vs 86.87) and Qwen3-4B, and AtP beats it on GPT-2 Large (142.03 vs 112.31). The authors say logit-level attribution misses negative name-mover heads.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient or decomposition attribution methods rank IOI-relevant components faithfully under zero-ablation disruption/recovery.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The IOI component tables report attribution AUCs without uncertainty estimates. The exact-patching comparison covers 200 samples and attention heads on one model, and the study says zero ablation may introduce out-of-distribution artifacts. LTP attributes logits rather than post-softmax probabilities and therefore misses suppressive effects; the authors also acknowledge approximation error on IOI.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant IOI component rows were omitted.

untested.parts: Entire version: no GPT-2 small circuit, head classes, or faithfulness/completeness/minimality tests.
Entire version: no name-mover ablation or backup-head analysis.
Entire version: IOI is run on other models only as an attribution benchmark, with no head classes or roles identified.
Entire version: no comparison of whether circuit-finding methods recover the same IOI circuit.
Entire version: no analysis of how the circuit's faithfulness or completeness depends on ablation, metric or prompt distribution.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's tests/T5 relation and its V4/V5 labels are wrong. The paper benchmarks its own attribution method and makes no claim about the IOI circuit. Several row values (r8, r9, r11, r12, r14, r15, r17, r18) were copied from the Known 1000 columns instead of the IOI columns.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test GPT-2 Small, the specific 26 attention heads or seven classes, their stated roles, or the authors' faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria for that circuit.
No ablation of the main name-mover heads or test of backup-head self-repair.
IOI attribution is evaluated on other models, but the study does not establish that the same head classes and roles carry IOI across models, checkpoints or tasks.

The study compares LTP with exact activation patching for attention-head rankings on one model and sample set. It does not compare circuit-finding methods, ablation types or metrics to establish recovery of the same circuit.
It discusses logit versus probability attribution and zero-ablation limitations, but does not systematically vary IOI prompt distributions or ablation types.
No comparison across name orders, templates or numbers of names.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: IOI attention-head rankings on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, especially top-ranked or causally effective heads
reader_labels.reason: LTP and exact activation patching show strong reported agreement on the top-20 overlap, Spearman correlation and effective-head sign agreement (r19-r22).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Full population of 1,024 attention heads on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
reader_labels.reason: The full-population Spearman correlation is lower, ρ = 0.39, so agreement is weaker beyond the heads with meaningful causal effects (r23).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: IOI component-attribution evaluations reported in the study
reader_labels.reason: The authors state that logit-level attribution structurally misses suppressive negative name-mover effects and that approximation errors occur on IOI; the GPT-2 Large recovery result also trails AtP in aggregate recovery (r1-r18).
